source_refs.note: Book p. 112: 6.9.1 definition of H.M., derivation H = 2ab/(a+b), example H.M. of 3 and 7 = 21/5. Teaching notes, comparison of means, key points and common mistakes are ours.

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein hum ne dekha ke H.P. asal mein ulti A.P. hai. Ab sawal yeh hai: agar do numbers diye hon, to un ke beech mein aisa kaun sa number rakhein ke teenon H.P. ban jayen? Isi beech wale number ko Harmonic Mean kehte hain. Aap A.M. aur G.M. pehle parh chuke hain; aaj teesra 'mean' seekhte hain.
Kitab ki definition: ek number \(H\) ko do numbers \(a\) aur \(b\) ke darmiyan harmonic mean (H.M.) kehte hain agar \(a, H, b\) H.P. mein hon.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kisi bhi 'mean' ka matlab hai do numbers ke beech mein fit hone wala aisa number jis se teenon ek progression ban jayen. A.P. ke liye yeh arithmetic mean \(A = \frac{a+b}{2}\) hai (seedha aadha jama), G.P. ke liye geometric mean \(G = \pm\sqrt{ab}\). Aur H.P. ke beech wale number ko harmonic mean kehte hain.
Ab chaabi wali baat: H.P. ke reciprocals A.P. hote hain. Is liye \(\frac{1}{H}\) zaroor \(\frac{1}{a}\) aur \(\frac{1}{b}\) ka arithmetic mean hoga. Neeche ki poori derivation isi ek khayal par khari hai.
Maan lijiye \(a, b\) do numbers hain aur \(H\) un ka H.M. hai. To \(\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{H}, \frac{1}{b}\) A.P. mein honge. Is liye:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(\frac{1}{H}\) in dono ka average kyun hai? A.P. mein beech wali term dono kinaron se barabar faasle par hoti hai: \(\frac{1}{H} - \frac{1}{a} = \frac{1}{b} - \frac{1}{H}\). Dono taraf \(\frac{1}{H} + \frac{1}{a}\) jama karein to \(\frac{2}{H} = \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b}\) milta hai, yani \(\frac{1}{H}\) = dono ka aadha jama.
Beech wala qadam fractions ko jama karna hai: common denominator \(ab\) le kar \(\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} = \frac{b}{ab} + \frac{a}{ab} = \frac{b+a}{ab}\). Phir \(2\) se divide karne ka matlab hai denominator ko \(2\) se multiply kar dena, is liye \(\frac{a+b}{2ab}\).
Ab dono taraf ka reciprocal (ulta) lein, to H.M. ka formula mil jata hai:

blocks.text_alt: H equals 2 a b over (a plus b)

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text:
Yeh formula tabhi chalta hai jab \(a 
e 0\), \(b 
e 0\) aur \(a + b 
e 0\) ho (warna neeche zero aa jaye ga). Yaad karne ka jumla: "do guna product, upar; sum, neeche". Agar sawal mein H.M. diya ho aur koi number poocha ho, to values is formula mein rakh kar equation hal kar lein.
Kitab ki misaal: \(3\) aur \(7\) ke darmiyan H.M. yeh hai:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Tasdeeq kar lete hain ke \(3, \frac{21}{5}, 7\) waqai H.P. mein hain: in ke reciprocals \(\frac{1}{3}, \frac{5}{21}, \frac{1}{7}\) hain, yani \(\frac{7}{21}, \frac{5}{21}, \frac{3}{21}\). Har dafa \(\frac{2}{21}\) kam ho raha hai, to yeh A.P. hai. Bilkul theek!
Ab \(3\) aur \(7\) ke teenon means ka muqabla dekhiye: \(A = 5\), \(G = \sqrt{21} \approx 4.58\), \(H = \frac{21}{5} = 4.2\). Do positive numbers ke liye hamesha \(A \ge G \ge H\) hota hai, aur \(G^{2} = AH\) (yahan \(5 \times 4.2 = 21\)). Yeh do baatein kitab ne yahan nahin likhin, yeh hamari taraf se hain, magar exercise ke un sawalon mein bohat kaam aati hain jahan A.M., G.M. aur H.M. ikatthe diye hon.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: \(4\) aur \(12\) ka H.M. nikaalein.
\(H = \frac{2 \times 4 \times 12}{4 + 12} = \frac{96}{16} = 6\).
Tasdeeq: reciprocals \(\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{6}, \frac{1}{12}\), yani \(\frac{3}{12}, \frac{2}{12}, \frac{1}{12}\): A.P. hai.
Saath mein \(A = 8\), \(G = \sqrt{48} \approx 6.93\), aur \(G^{2} = 48 = 8 \times 6 = AH\).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar \(a = b\) ho, maslan \(5\) aur \(5\), to H.M. kya hoga? Formula: \(\frac{2 \times 25}{10} = 5\). Yani jab dono numbers barabar hon to teenon means (A, G, H) bhi wahi number ban jate hain. Kya aap bata sakte hain ke \(2\) aur \(-2\) ka H.M. kyun nahin nikal sakta? (Ishara: \(a + b\) dekhiye.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(H\) number \(a\) aur \(b\) ka H.M. hai jab \(a, H, b\) H.P. mein hon.
2. Is ka matlab \(\frac{1}{H}\) number \(\frac{1}{a}\) aur \(\frac{1}{b}\) ka A.M. hai.
3. \(H = \frac{2ab}{a+b}\), shart: \(a, b, a+b \ne 0\).
4. Positive numbers ke liye: \(A \ge G \ge H\) aur \(G^{2} = AH\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(H = \frac{a+b}{2ab}\) likh dena: yeh to \(\frac{1}{H}\) hai; aakhir mein ulta karna zaroori hai.
2. \(\frac{2}{a+b}\) (product \(ab\) bhool gaye) ya \(\frac{ab}{a+b}\) (\(2\) bhool gaye) likhna. Bachne ke liye har dafa \(3\) aur \(7\) wali misaal se formula check kar lein: jawab \(\frac{21}{5}\) aana chahiye.
3. Yeh samajhna ke H.M. seedha A.M. ka reciprocal hai: \(3\) aur \(7\) ke liye yeh \(\frac{1}{5}\) dega, jab ke H.M. \(\frac{21}{5}\) hai.
